apk_origin: OWASP MASTG / Crackmes / Android / Level_04 (Radare2 r2pay-v1.0 — fictional payment crackme)
scope_note: Pipeline boundary case — like UnCrackable-Level2 but with stronger Java-side anti-tamper. Token generation is entirely native (gXftm3iswpkVgBNDUp in libnative-lib.so). Java side adds RootBeer-based root detection + intentional ArithmeticException ('1337/0') as a tamper-response. None of the patterns map to result_schema.json category enum. Stage 1 in-scope findings = 0.
negative_confirmations: Token generation runs in native-lib (libnative-lib.so) via gXftm3iswpkVgBNDUp(byte[], byte). Java side passes input + flag, receives byte array — no plaintext crypto in Java.

RootBeer (com.scottyab.rootbeer) used for root detection — a third-party utility, not a vulnerability in itself. Library is properly invoked with both `isRooted()` and the native-side `isRootedWithBusyBoxCheck()` path.
Anti-tamper response: int i = 1337 / 0 (ArithmeticException) + np.notify() on a fresh NullPointerException — both intentional crash-by-side-effect patterns. Not in category enum.
No Cipher / MessageDigest / SecretKeySpec / KeyStore in Java. No HTTP / WebView / external network. No hardcoded secrets at the regex tier (no AKIA*, sk_live_*, PRIVATE KEY block).
No exported components. ContentProvider/Receiver/Service definitions absent.
out_of_scope_findings: Native PIN/amount validation in libnative-lib.so. Recoverable via radare2 / Ghidra binary analysis. — MASVS-CRYPTO-1 / MASVS-AUTH-2.
Tamper-response design: 1337/0 + NullPointerException.notify() patterns can be patched with Frida (replace System.exit / hook Throwable). — MASVS-RESILIENCE-3.
RootBeer's root-detection heuristics are bypassable via standard root-cloaking tools (MagiskHide, Zygisk). — MASVS-RESILIENCE-3.
